Main file: four examples. Table 1 (p.4, NETL-401, 2007): ONE example (process 'BGL gasification plants, NETL-401 (Table 1)', gasifier_coal) with two coal-quality cases named in square brackets in each note - Illinois No. 6 bituminous and Wyodak sub-bituminous - with capacity (syngas GJ/h, product-output), net efficiency, capex, fixed O&M (derived per GJ/yr of capacity from the printed M$/yr, formula given), variable O&M. Table 2 (p.5, summary): syngas (gasifier_coal), syngas with ~20% H2 via PSA (gasifier_coal_hydrogen-coproduction) and SNG (gasifier_coal_methanation), with construction time, lifetime, load factor, emissions and - for the H2 and SNG columns - capacity, efficiency, capex, fixed and variable O&M. The Table 2 syngas column is only the range of the two Table 1 plants, so its capacity/efficiency/cost cells are NOT loaded (sidecar _summary-restatements); only the cells Table 2 adds are on that technology. CAPEX BASIS: '$/GJ output' is per GJ/yr of product output at 8,760 h (verified: 118.7 M$ / (1005 GJ/h x 8760) = 13.48); unit 2005_USD/GJ-per-yr, CAPACITY BASIS product-output, COST BASIS total-plant. Fixed O&M is on the same basis, unit 2005_USD/GJ-per-yr (annual cost per GJ/yr of capacity, per year; no trailing /yr). The syngas+H2 capacity is the printed 210-310 MWth (thermal-output); no hand-summed syngas+H2 total is recorded. Rerun 2026-09-25 under the current rules (output etsap3). NUMBER FORMAT: Table 2 and parts of the text use European decimal commas and thousands dots ('17,2', '1.200', '20.700', '7,4 Mt/y', '930-1.030 t/d'); all transcribed as ordinary decimals. Ranges printed high-to-low are stored min<max with a note. No flows file: the source gives only hourly rates, and the coal/syngas ratio (85%) does not reproduce the stated net efficiency (74.7%). Sidecars (not loaded): _summary-restatements, _throughputs (MWth ratings, hourly coal, H2SO4, plant totals), _projections (2020/2030/2050 efficiency and capex), _ccs-cost-adders (Table 2 CCS and transport/storage rows, IEA 2006/2005 text), _economics-and-market (levelized production costs, coal prices, relative costs, location factors, market figures). Omitted: gasifier type descriptions (moving, fluidized, entrained) and operating temperatures/pressures, which are generic and not for the BGL system.

(1) 'Gasif. capacity, output' in MWth does not equal the syngas output: Illinois 310 MWth vs 1005 GJ/h = 279 MW; Wyodak 207 vs 671 GJ/h = 186 MW; SNG 170-260 MWth vs 560-840 GJ/h = 156-233 MW. The cost denominators follow the GJ/h output, not the MWth figure. (2) Net efficiency (74.7%, 72.8%) is not reproducible from Table 1's coal feed and syngas output (85.2%, 83.7%). (3) Table 1 'Tot. plant cost' has no unit (millions of US$ by arithmetic). (4) p.1 Highlights give the bituminous capital cost as '$13/GJ'; the body and Table 1 say 13.5. (5) Table 2 uses European decimal commas and thousands dots, while Table 1 on the previous page uses decimal points; the text mixes both ('930-1.030 t/d', '7,4 Mt/y'). (6) Table 2 ranges are printed high-to-low, and the order is not consistent: fixed O&M reads '1,0 - 0,7' (syngas), '0,7 - 1,0' (syngas/H2) and '1,6 - 0,8' (SNG). (7) 'Load factor and availability, %' merges two parameters in one row. (8) 'Capital cost, $/GJ output' is per GJ/yr of capacity at 8,760 h ('$/GJa' in the text), easily misread as a levelized per-GJ cost. (9) Table 2 transport & storage of CO2 '$6-20/t' conflicts with the p.4 text ($1-10 transport per 100 km plus $2-10 storage and monitoring = $3-20). (10) The Table 2 syngas column restates Table 1 (rounded: 207 MWth printed as 210). (11) Typo 'cola' for coal (p.3); 'decreases by over 14% percentage points' (p.4). (12) Projection capex cells break across two lines ('16,2 - / 12,5'), which plain-text extraction splits into separate rows. (13) Emission factors are per 'PJ total output' without saying whether the CO2 is from combustion or the process vent.
